  "scenario": "A logistics company runs nightly inventory audit exports from a SQLite database to a CSV with running balances per warehouse. The export tool supports checkpoint/resume for long-running jobs, but staff report that when they stop a run and resume it later, the resulting CSV differs from what a single uninterrupted run would produce. The tool must be fixed so a resumed export is identical to an uninterrupted one.",
  "environment_setup": "The Dockerfile builds a Python 3.12 image with /app as WORKDIR. setup_db.py creates /app/warehouse.db with ~217 transactions across 5 warehouses (ALPHA, BETA, CENTRAL, DELTA, GAMMA) over January 2024, with interleaved IDs so the (warehouse_id, date, id) sort order diverges from numeric id order. setup_db.py is deleted after build. The main tool is /app/audit_export.py (~300 lines), a structured CLI tool with BalanceTracker, CheckpointManager, and AuditExporter classes. It reads transactions sorted by (warehouse_id, tx_date, id), computes running balances, writes CSV rows plus a summary section, and supports --checkpoint / --resume / --limit flags. A config.ini and README.md document usage. Four bugs are planted in the resume path: (1) running balances are never saved to or restored from the checkpoint, (2) the resume query filters by id > last_id but the export sorts by (warehouse_id, tx_date, id), so records with lower ids that sort later are skipped and records with higher ids that sort earlier are duplicated, (3) the CSV header is written unconditionally even when appending on resume, and the old summary section from the interrupted run is not removed before appending, and (4) checkpoints are only saved every BATCH_SIZE (25) records, so stopping at a non-batch-boundary (e.g. --limit 37) means the checkpoint lags behind and records between the last checkpoint and the stop point are duplicated on resume. Each bug is an omission or mismatch in the interaction between components; no single function is wrong on its own.",
  "instruction_summary": "Fix /app/audit_export.py so that a resumed export produces exactly the same output as an uninterrupted export. The tool reads from /app/warehouse.db and writes a CSV to a specified --output path. With --checkpoint, it saves progress; with --resume, it continues. A resumed export must produce a CSV with the same header, the same transaction rows in the same order with the same running-balance values, and the same summary section as a full uninterrupted run. The invariant must hold regardless of when the export is interrupted and resumed. The README at /app/README.md documents the tool's interface and output format.",
  "solution_outline": [
    "Add last_warehouse_id and last_tx_date fields to CheckpointManager.save and the checkpoint JSON",
    "Add a balances dict to the checkpoint JSON, populated from BalanceTracker.to_dict()",
    "Change _build_query to accept last_wh/last_date/last_id and use WHERE (warehouse_id, tx_date, id) > (?, ?, ?) instead of WHERE id > ?",
    "In export(), on resume: load checkpoint, restore balances via BalanceTracker.from_dict(), truncate the output file before the '# Summary' marker (and preceding blank line) to remove the old summary, and skip writing the CSV header when appending",
    "Save a final checkpoint (with all fields including balances) just before writing the summary, and also just before the --limit break, so the checkpoint is always current when the tool stops"
  ],

Tests also use a --limit that is NOT a multiple of the batch size (37), ensuring a solution that only fixes batch-boundary resumption fails.",
  "failure_modes": "An agent may fix the resume query (fault 2) and verify record counts match, but miss that balances restart from zero (fault 1). The batch-boundary checkpoint gap is a classic off-by-one variant but in a novel context (resume after partial batch). None of these reproduce a named CVE, blog post, or textbook exercise.",
  "static_read": "Reading each function in isolation, everything looks reasonable: CheckpointManager.save correctly persists what it's told; _build_query correctly filters by the id it receives; BalanceTracker correctly accumulates; write_header writes a header. The bugs only emerge when tracing data flow: what does the checkpoint capture vs what does the export need to resume? The checkpoint captures an id; the export needs a (warehouse, date, id) tuple. The checkpoint omits balances; the export depends on accumulated balances. The file-append path writes a header; the file already has one. The batch timer saves checkpoints; but the tool can stop between timers.",
  "crux": "A checkpoint for a stateful, ordered export must capture every piece of accumulated state (running balances) and must use a resume key that is co-prime with the export's sort order (tuple comparison, not just primary key), and must be saved at every exit point, not just at periodic batch boundaries.",
  "challenge_kind": "resume_after_interruption",
  "sequence_invariant": "Regardless of when an export is stopped and resumed, the final output CSV must contain exactly the same header, transaction rows (in the same order with the same balance values), and summary section as an uninterrupted run from the same database.",
  "nameable_fix": "Checkpoint the balance state and resume using the sort-order tuple",
  "self_check_blind_spot": "After fixing the resume query (fault 2), the agent re-runs with --limit 50 and verifies all transaction IDs are present and the row count matches. This passes. But balances for warehouses with pre-checkpoint transactions are still wrong (fault 1), the file has a duplicate header (fault 3), and if they later test with --limit 37 they'd see duplicates (fault 4). The natural re-test (count rows, check a few IDs) does not reveal faults 1, 3, or 4.",
  "reference_in_environment": "None. The BalanceTracker class has to_dict/from_dict methods that serialize balance state, but they are never called and do not constitute a reference implementation of correct checkpointing. The README states the resume invariant but not how to achieve it. No test files, no .git history, no backup copies exist in the image.",
  "interaction": "The central defect arises from the interaction between (A) CheckpointManager, which persists a resume key (last_processed_id) and batch count, and (B) AuditExporter, which processes records in (warehouse_id, tx_date, id) order and accumulates balances in a BalanceTracker. Each component is internally consistent: the checkpoint saves 'where we left off' by id, and the exporter sorts and accumulates correctly. But the checkpoint's notion of 'where' uses a different coordinate system (id) than the exporter's sort order (warehouse_id, tx_date, id), and the checkpoint omits the exporter's accumulated state (balances). A third interaction: the file-open logic (append mode on resume) assumes the output file's existing content is just transaction rows, but the interrupted run also wrote a summary section and header that must be accounted for. A fourth: the batch-timer checkpoint logic assumes the tool always stops at a batch boundary, but --limit can stop it mid-batch."
